summary: Tipperary-born son of Humphrey Heffernan, transported to New South Wales after the 1834 killing of a constable at Ballynonty; John's 4th-great-grand-uncle.
bio: James Heffernan was baptized in 1812 in County Tipperary, a son of Humphrey Heffernan and Anastasia Ryan. In 1834 he, his brother Patrick and others were convicted of manslaughter over the killing of a constable named Feeney at Ballynonty, and he was transported to New South Wales for seven years. He was probably John's 4th-great-grand-uncle.
sources: Michael Dwyer, Heffernans of Slieveardagh (Welsh Hill Press, 2020), Branch 4 (and Branch 3), working from the Killenaule and Gortnahoe Catholic parish registers: https://archive.org/details/heffernans-of-slieveardagh
